bank.q: Arrange the following in correct chronological order:
items: Golak Nath v. State of Punjab
First sitting of the Constituent Assembly
bank.e: Government of India Act 1935 → first sitting of the Constituent Assembly, 9 December 1946 → Shankari Prasad, 1951 → Golak Nath, 1967.

bank.q: Consider the following statements tracing continuity from colonial rule to constitutional democracy:
s: The Federal Court of the 1935 Act was the institutional predecessor of the Supreme Court, which later invented the Basic Structure Doctrine.
The three-fold division of legislative powers under the 1935 Act survives as the Seventh Schedule, and federalism is now a basic feature.
The 1935 Act's ordinance power was abandoned by the Constitution as incompatible with responsible government.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — the ordinance power was retained, becoming Articles 123 and 213.

bank.as: The body that adopted universal adult suffrage was not itself elected by universal adult suffrage, and the body that first amended the Constitution was not elected by the people at all.
bank.rs: The Constituent Assembly was indirectly elected by provincial legislatures, and the First Amendment was passed by the Provisional Parliament.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. This democratic-legitimacy gap is one of the standard critiques of the First Amendment and the Ninth Schedule.

bank.q: Match List I (constitutional moment) with List II (its immediate consequence):
pairs: 2. Article 15(4) inserted by the First Amendment
C. Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain (1975)
3. The 42nd Amendment attempted to nullify judicial limits
bank.e: Champakam triggered Article 15(4); Golak Nath triggered the 24th Amendment's Articles 13(4) and 368(3); Indira Gandhi struck down the 39th; Kesavananda provoked the 42nd Amendment's attempt at nullification.

bank.q: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: Kesavananda was a thirteen-judge bench and Coelho a nine-judge bench
Waman Rao fixed 24 April 1973 as the cut-off for Ninth Schedule challenges
Minerva Mills struck down Articles 368(4) and 368(5)
The 44th Amendment restored Article 31 as a Fundamental Right
bank.e: The 44th Amendment removed property from Part III and inserted Article 300A. Nothing has restored Article 31.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about the relationship between amendment power and judicial review:
s: Shankari Prasad and Sajjan Singh held that a constitutional amendment is not law under Article 13(2).
Golak Nath reversed that position and was itself negatived by the 24th Amendment.
Kesavananda restored the Golak Nath position that Part III cannot be amended at all.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Kesavananda did not restore Golak Nath — it overruled it, upholding the 24th Amendment while subjecting all amendments to the basic structure.

bank.q: Which of the following best captures the difference between the width test and the identity test?
o: Width concerns procedure; identity concerns substance
Width concerns the scope of power used; identity concerns qualitative transformation of the constitutional order
Width applies to ordinary laws; identity applies to amendments
Width is textual; identity is judge-made
bank.e: The width test asks how far the amendment's reach extends; the identity test asks whether the document that emerges is still the same Constitution.

bank.q: All of the following are recognised as part of the basic structure EXCEPT:
o: The objectives specified in the Preamble
bank.e: The Fifth Schedule is a temporary provision that does not require an Article 368 amendment — SC AoR Association (1994).

bank.as: The basic structure doctrine is described as the juridical operationalisation of constitutional morality.
bank.rs: The doctrine supplies the mechanism while constitutional morality supplies the normative content of what counts as basic.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. This is the bridge between the technical doctrine and the larger moral architecture of the Constitution.

bank.q: Which sequence correctly describes the fate of the Preamble's status?
o: Part of the Constitution (1950) → not part (1960) → part again (1973)
Not part (1960) → integral source (1973) → objectives protected as basic structure
Basic structure (1973) → amendable in text (1976) → non-amendable (1980)
bank.e: Berubari (1960) said it was not part of the Constitution; Kesavananda (1973) made it an integral source; its objectives now carry basic-structure protection even though its text was amended in 1976.
